vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-rate-limiter
Version: 1.2.0

The OpenClaw AgentSkills skill bundle 'agent-rate-limiter' is classified as benign. The Python script `scripts/rate-limiter.py` securely manages its local state file (`rate-limit-state.json`) using file locking (`fcntl.flock`), atomic writes, and restricted file permissions (0o600). It includes robust input validation for command-line arguments and path validation to prevent directory traversal. There are no external network calls, no dynamic code execution from untrusted sources, and no attempts to access sensitive system data or establish persistence. The `SKILL.md` documentation provides clear instructions for the AI agent to use the rate limiter, and these instructions do not contain any malicious prompt injection attempts, instead focusing solely on the skill's intended functionality.

llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and optional environment variables are consistent with a local, file-backed rate limiter for agent workflows; there is no evidence of network exfiltration, unrelated credential requests, or unexpected installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim a local rate-limiter; the package contains a Python script and a JSON state file implementing exactly that behavior. Optional env vars (RATE_LIMIT_*) match configuration needs. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or downloads are requested.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs placing gate/record calls in agent loops and optionally adding text to AGENTS.md / the system prompt. That is appropriate for a rate-limiter, but reviewers should be aware the guidance includes editing agent/system prompts (a deliberate global change). A pre-scan 'system-prompt-override' pattern was detected — in context the SKILL.md asks maintainers to insert gate calls into the system prompt/agent config rather than covertly overriding prompts, but you should apply those changes manually and review them before applying.

Note: default state file path resolves to the parent directory of the script (../rate-limit-state.json) — confirm this location is acceptable for your environment and permissions.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: a local, file-backed rate limiter with no external network calls or credential access. Before installing: 1) Review and test scripts locally (run python3 scripts/rate-limiter.py gate; record; status). 2) Confirm the state file location (default resolves to ../rate-limit-state.json) and set RATE_LIMIT_STATE to a path you control; check file permissions. 3) Note the script uses fcntl/flock (Unix-only semantics) — it may not behave correctly on Windows. 4) When integrating into agent/system prompts, edit prompts/config manually and avoid blindly applying automated prompt changes. 5) Run in a safe test agent first to ensure the gate/exit-code behavior matches your orchestration and avoids unintended halts. If you want extra assurance, review the remainder of the truncated code paths (full file) for any unexpected subprocess/network usage before deploying widely.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] expected: Scanner flagged a pattern that could indicate attempt to override system prompts. In this skill, SKILL.md explicitly recommends adding gate/record checks to AGENTS.md / system prompt so that the agent uses the rate limiter. That recommendation is expected for this purpose, but treat it as an instruction you should apply manually and review rather than allow automated modification.
